green_summary.2.1.a_shared_contracts: contracts/delivery/schema-kernel.js + eight *.schema.js + index.js registry. Handwritten zero-dependency validators (node builtins only, tools/infra fail-closed style). Compat boundary: payload.schemaVersion mandatory; > version rejected as 'newer than supported', < version rejected as 'older than supported — no compatibility mapping declared', missing/non-integer rejected; unknown contract names refused by parseContract with the registered set listed. Field-level errors with paths (e.g. release.commit, executionDenominator.totalCases, must be one of product|design|usecase). Semantic fail-closed rule beyond structure: ReleaseReceipt requires readback.ok === true.
green_summary.2.1.b_full_input_baseline: lib/delivery/baseline.js. computeFullInputBaseline digests six declared groups (sources/tests/lockfiles/migrations/deployConfigs/artifacts) — non-JS inputs (.java/.py/.sql/.yaml) bind the digest, per A08; any declared-but-missing file returns error=MISSING_INPUT with the sorted missing list (explicit scope error, never silent). taskDefinitionDigest normalizes [x]/[ ] so progress checkboxes cannot move the frozen definition digest. traceAcToCases lists exact missing acceptance mappings. requireImplementationBaselines refuses implementation dispatch listing missing product/design/usecase (A01). invalidateOnScopeChange invalidates only receipts bound to the changed baseline kind, on digest drift or revision drift, keeping unrelated receipts valid (A02). verifyReportCurrency returns DIGEST_MISMATCH with bound vs current digest (A07).
green_summary.2.1.c_valid_red_and_denominator: lib/delivery/test-contract.js. parseTapSummary reads the top-level TAP summary (nested suite summaries cannot shadow it). classifyRunOutcome: spawnError or known environment signatures (module-not-found, ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT family, ENOENT/EACCES, spawn failures) or missing TAP summary => environment-failure (conservative fail-closed: doubtful runs must be re-executed, never trusted); tests==0 or pass+fail==0 => empty; fail>0 without signatures => behavior-red; exit code contradicting a passing summary => environment-failure. evaluateExecutionDenominator refuses 'zero tests executed' and 'zero effective executions: N skipped, M cancelled'. requireValidRed accepts only behavior-red with a real executed count and refuses environment/empty/pass runs with explicit reasons. evaluateExecution validates the TestContract through the schema and refuses acceptance unless the run is a real passing execution meeting the declared denominator ('execution denominator unmet: declared N, observed M'); observed counts always come from run output, so declared numbers alone cannot close the behavior.

test_fixes_between_red_and_green.finding: four RED-phase test corrections were needed before GREEN
test_fixes_between_red_and_green.details: (1) test/delivery-baseline.test.js asserted 6 manifest files where DEMO_MANIFEST lists 7 (authoring arithmetic error, implementation was correct); (2) expected missing-list order assumed locale sort while the implementation uses deterministic code-unit sort — expectation corrected to the implementation's documented order; (3) frozen-contract list compared unsorted against Object.keys().sort() — comparison now sorts both sides; (4) test/delivery-cases/2_1.mjs runNodeTest inherited NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8 from the outer node --test, which makes a nested node --test skip running files entirely (exit 0, no TAP output — captured during debugging); the fixture now strips that variable so spawned runs are real top-level executions. None of these weaken an oracle; one genuine implementation bug found the same way (evaluateExecution initially dropped denominator.reasons from the rejection list) was fixed in lib/delivery/test-contract.js.

schema validates structure only, by design: per delivery-architecture.md section 4, digest proves content binding, not origin trust; source attestation and registered-runner checks are 2.2 scope. The EvidenceEnvelope/GateReceipt sourceAttestation fields are structural placeholders for that gate.

blockers_or_questions: The conservative environment-failure classifier is intentionally fail-closed: a legitimate behavior RED whose captured output happens to contain a signature substring (e.g. asserting on 'ENOENT' text) classifies as environment failure and blocks RED recording rather than fabricating one. If 2.2/P3_1 need finer separation (signature scoped to the failure location rather than the whole output), that is a follow-up on top of classifyRunOutcome, not a scope change.

test/delivery-cases/2_1.mjs is deliberately outside the npm test glob (matches repo pattern: test/*.test.js only); it runs via the explicit node --test command recorded above and later through the P3_1 verify runner. Reviewers should run the explicit command, not expect it in npm test.
